title: Protracted displacement is being managed as a long-term social and development-system problem while humanitarian funding remains structurally inadequate
geography: Global forced displacement and statelessness across 128 countries and territories, including host communities and displacement-affected areas

denominator.unit: people projected to be forcibly displaced or stateless in 2026

operational_presence.unit: countries and territories where UNHCR plans to be present and undertake action

funding_requirement.unit: billion US dollars needed in 2026 to protect and assist forcibly displaced and stateless people

system_condition.value: Displacement is framed as involving uncertainty, vulnerability, legal recognition, safety, services, and access to opportunity rather than only emergency shelter

observations.method: UNHCR annual global appeal using projected populations, country and regional operational plans, programmatic priorities, and financial requirements.
observations.uncertainty: The 136 million figure is a planning projection and the $8.505 billion figure is an appeal requirement, not realized displacement, funding received, or outcome measurement.
observations.subgroup: Refugees, asylum-seekers, internally displaced people, stateless people, returnees, host communities, women, children, and people with disabilities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A very large operational footprint can signal institutional reach while also revealing how displacement has become normalized and how humanitarian systems may be asked to substitute for political resolution.

funding_model.value: Humanitarian funding alone is described as insufficient for unprecedented and protracted displacement

development_partnership.value: UNHCR is increasingly working with development actors such as the World Bank to support solutions and sustain government-led responses

host_system_focus.value: The strategy emphasizes displacement-affected areas and equitable access to services for displaced people and host communities

observations.method: UNHCR strategic appeal linking protection and assistance to development actors, national systems, host-community services, and longer-term solutions.
observations.uncertainty: The strategy does not prove that development partnerships will be adequately financed, locally legitimate, or capable of replacing emergency resources in acute crises.
observations.subgroup: Host governments, municipalities, service providers, development institutions, refugees, displaced people, stateless people, and host communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Embedding displacement response in national and development systems can improve durability, but it can also dilute protection obligations or shift responsibility onto already-constrained host services.

denominator.unit: UNHCR Global Appeal 2026 policy and program agenda

legal_policy_route.value: The appeal calls for improved legal and policy environments and protection-sensitive responses for people forced to flee

economic_inclusion_route.value: The agenda includes access to employment, entrepreneurship, agribusiness, and financial services for forcibly displaced and stateless people

service_route.value: Equitable access to services in displacement-affected areas is treated as a key investment area

observations.method: UNHCR global planning framework combining protection, services, livelihoods, economic inclusion, and solutions priorities.
observations.uncertainty: Policy commitments and program priorities do not establish legal access, work authorization, service uptake, income security, or durable self-reliance for affected people.
observations.subgroup: Forcibly displaced and stateless people, host communities, employers, financial-service providers, farmers, entrepreneurs, and public agencies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Economic inclusion can increase agency and reduce dependency, but labor-market access without rights, bargaining power, or adequate services can produce low-paid and precarious integration.

denominator.unit: UNHCR Global Appeal 2026 focus-area routes shown in the public planning interface

route_set.value: The appeal organizes country and regional planning around access, status, policy, gender-based violence, children, justice, community, basic needs, shelter, health, education, WASH, livelihoods, returns, resettlement, and local solutions

multi_stage_problem.value: Protection and durable solutions require linked legal, social, health, education, livelihood, shelter, and local-capacity stages

coordination_requirement.value: The appeal requires coordination among governments, UNHCR, development actors, civil society, communities, and other partners

observations.method: UNHCR public appeal architecture and operational planning categories.
observations.uncertainty: A planning taxonomy shows intended coverage, not that every route is funded, available, accessible, safe, or connected for each person or place.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people and host communities moving through different protection, service, status, work, return, resettlement, and local-solution pathways.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multi-stage framework can prevent narrow emergency metrics, but a large route architecture can also fragment accountability and make it difficult to observe whether people experience a coherent path to safety and opportunity.

boundary: This record adds a global displacement-and-capacity signal linking forced displacement, statelessness, humanitarian funding, host systems, legal recognition, services, work, economic inclusion, and durable solutions. It is a UNHCR planning appeal, not a realized displacement count, funding-outcome evaluation, respondent-level dataset, or proof that economic inclusion and development partnerships produce durable protection or agency.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNHCR Global Appeal 2026 page reviewed for projected displaced/stateless population, countries and territories, funding requirement, humanitarian-to-development shift, equitable services, legal and policy environments, economic inclusion priorities, and operational focus areas.
